title: Lesson 54 - When OmniStudio Is and Is Not the Right Fit in the System Landscape
description: Justify and recommend architectural choices, demonstrating how OmniStudio components fit into the overall Salesforce and enterprise system landscape.

questions.question: A team needs to move data from an external system into Salesforce as part of a nightly process. Which approach is the best fit?
options: An OmniScript that a user runs each night
An Integration Procedure invoked on a schedule
An Apex batch job or platform event driven integration
A FlexCard that displays the external data
questions.explanation: A scheduled, high-volume data load is a background integration, which belongs to Apex batch or platform events, not to user-facing OmniStudio components. An OmniScript requires a user to run it and is not built for volume. An Integration Procedure is request-response and not designed for scheduled bulk loads. A FlexCard only displays data and does not move it.

questions.question: The same external lookup is needed by three different OmniScripts. Where should the lookup logic live?
options: In a single shared Integration Procedure
In a custom setting that stores the response
In a FlexCard that each script embeds
questions.explanation: A shared Integration Procedure centralizes the external call and transformation so all three OmniScripts reuse one tested artifact. Duplicating the logic in each script creates drift and maintenance burden. A custom setting stores configuration, not a live lookup result. A FlexCard is a display component, not a service for OmniScripts to call.

questions.question: An architect is evaluating a guided multi-step claim intake flow that will be used by a small team of adjusters. What is the strongest reason to choose an OmniScript?
options: It is the only way to build a form in Salesforce
It runs faster than any other option at high volume
It provides a guided, stateful journey with built-in data handling under the user's context
It requires no security configuration because it bypasses sharing rules
questions.explanation: An OmniScript is purpose-built for guided, stateful journeys and handles data under the user's context, which matches a small-team claim intake. It is not the only way to build a form, so that reason is false. It is not optimized for high volume, so that reason is also false. It does not bypass sharing rules; it runs under them, so the last option is incorrect.
